requirements.statement: A visually hidden polite live region announces how many species a typed search lists, reading '3 results available' for three and '1 result available' for one, and 'No results found' when none match, and announces nothing while the typed search is shorter than three characters.
requirements.why: Results that change as the trader types must be announced to screen reader users.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-060 and -p9-061 hold the count announcement, its singular form, its no-results form and the silence below three characters; trace-e2e-p5-020 captured the earlier server-written panel with no live region (c-commodities-001).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, ticking a species adds it to the chosen panel at once with focus left on the tick box, the typed search text and its results stay on screen so more species can be ticked, and removing one chosen species or clearing them all updates the page in place and puts focus back in the search box with the typed text still there.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader tick several species from one search without losing the search or the selection.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-064 and -p9-065 show the tick, the kept search text and the in-place update with focus returned to the search box; trace-animals-fit-p8-019 captured the earlier server round trip (c-commodities-001).

requirements.statement: Search results list commodities alphabetically by commodity name, and the species under each alphabetically by their label ('common name (Latin name)', or 'commodity name (Latin name)' where a species has no common name).

How a list reads, its order included, follows the prototype, and a reference list is never a reason to block a row (ruling 11 November), so the order is not held back by the commodity list's content.

requirements.statement: In the search results the text that matched the query is shown in bold, in both the commodity header and the species labels (for example 'Domestic **cattle** (Bos taurus)').

requirements.statement: Search results are grouped under a header naming the commodity and its code ('Cattle (0102)'), falling back to the bare code where the commodity list holds no name for it, with a GOV.UK checkbox per species, and a query that matches a commodity's name or code lists every species of that commodity.
